codes.state_code: 2-digit Census 2011 state code as text ('01' J&K ... '35' A&N). 35 States/UTs as of 2011.
codes.district_code: 3-digit Census 2011 district code as text, '001'..'640', UNIQUE across India (nested contiguously within states, e.g. Karnataka 29 = 555..584, Bangalore = 572). Join key for the 2011 district boundary file.
2011_geography_quirks: ANDHRA PRADESH (28) = undivided AP; its first 10 districts 532-541 (Adilabad, Nizamabad, Karimnagar, Medak, Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Mahbubnagar, Nalgonda, Warangal, Khammam) are today's Telangana; 542-554 are residual AP
JAMMU & KASHMIR (01) includes Leh(Ladakh) 003 and Kargil 004
DAMAN & DIU (25) and DADRA & NAGAR HAVELI (26) are separate UTs
640 districts of 2011; many have since been split/renamed - seats must map to their 2011 parent district
State names are upper-case as in the source ('NCT OF DELHI', 'ANDAMAN & NICOBAR ISLANDS'); district names are the census spellings (whitespace collapsed only)

Duplicate district names across states: Aurangabad (BR 235 / MH 515), Bijapur (CG 417 / KA 557), Bilaspur (HP 030 / CG 406), Hamirpur (HP 028 / UP 168), Pratapgarh (RJ 131 / UP 173), Raigarh (CG 403 / MH 520) - always join on code or (state, name)

senapati_note: Senapati (Manipur, 272) includes ORGI's ESTIMATED population for Mao-Maram, Paomata and Purul sub-districts (TOT_P 285,404; P_ST 264,682; P_LIT 140,295; P_06 37,103; all rural). India/Manipur totals in this file include them (TOT_P 1,210,854,977). The commonly quoted ST 104,281,034 and literates 763,498,517 are the figures EXCLUDING these three sub-districts; this file gives 104,545,716 and 763,638,812. Both reconcile exactly.
